nodeTable.billingCycleTips:
Billing Cycle Rules

By Preset Cycle (Calendar Renewal)
When the number of days entered is close to the preset plan (such as monthly, quarterly, annually), it will renew according to the corresponding calendar cycle.
- Common values: 30 (monthly), 92 (quarterly), 365 (annually), 730 (biennially), etc.
- Example: Entering 30, the service renews on March 15, and the new expiration date will be April 15.

By Custom Days
When other numbers of days are entered (such as 7, 45, 100), it will strictly renew according to the number of days.
- Example: Entering 45, the service renews on March 15, and the new expiration date will be April 29 (45 days later).

One-time Payment
Entering -1 indicates a one-time payment.

chart.cutPeak_tips:
Tips on Data Smoothing

When you enable smoothing, the curves you see in the statistical charts are processed using the Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) algorithm, a commonly used data smoothing technique.


It's important to note that the values displayed by the EWMA algorithm's smoothed curves, are not the original, raw measured data. They represent a smoothed trend line calculated based on the EWMA algorithm, designed to reduce data fluctuations and make data patterns and trends easier to identify.


Therefore, the values you see are more of a visual presentation, helping you better understand the overall direction and long-term trends of the data, rather than the precise true value at each point in time. If you need to view specific, raw data points, please refer to the unsmoothed data view.

chart.loss_tips: Packet loss rate calculation algorithms are inaccurate; please use with caution. Vol(volatility): The tail fluctuation of latency, the higher the value, the greater the fluctuation, calculation method: (P99 - P50) / max(min(P50, 50), 10).
chart.samplingAlgorithmTips:
Downsampling
For historical ranges, the backend groups points into fixed time buckets aligned to the query interval, then calculates one value per bucket with the selected algorithm.

Average/Min/Max/First/Last/StdDev and percentile options all run on the values inside each bucket. Empty buckets stay empty, so gaps in the chart still mean missing data.

metrics.dsn_description: Connection string of the currently running monitoring database. The database type is detected automatically from the connection string (SQLite / MariaDB / MySQL / PostgreSQL). SQLite: ./data/metrics.db; MariaDB / MySQL: user:password@tcp(host:3306)/metrics?charset=utf8mb4&parseTime=True; PostgreSQL: host=localhost user=komari password=secret dbname=metrics port=5432 sslmode=disable
metrics.intro: Configure the monitoring database and the retention policy for each monitored metric's raw data.
metrics.max_idle_conns_description: Maximum number of idle database connections, default 5
metrics.max_open_conns_description: Maximum number of open database connections, default 25
metrics.migration_canceled_hint: Migration canceled. Since writes are idempotent, you can safely restart the migration without producing duplicate data.
metrics.migration_card_description: Move historical data from a monitoring data source database (the default local SQLite ./data/metrics.db, or the previously used database) into the currently running monitoring target database.
metrics.migration_completed_hint: Migration completed. All historical data has been moved to the current target database.
metrics.migration_failed_hint: Migration failed. Check the source/target database connection and server logs, then start the migration again.
metrics.migration_in_progress_hint: Migration is running. The server continues to operate normally. Large datasets may take a while.
metrics.restart_hint: Some changes only take effect after the service is restarted.
metrics.retention_description: Number of days to keep data, default 1; 0 disables persistence for the metric
metrics.retention_invalid: Please enter a valid number of days
metrics.retention_table_description: Set raw-data retention days for each monitoring metric. Default retention is {{days}} days. Set to 0 to disable persistence for the metric.
metrics.retention_warning_description: With downsampling disabled, retaining more than one day writes every raw Agent sample to the database and can quickly increase database size and slow queries. Enable downsampling when possible; use an external MariaDB, MySQL, or PostgreSQL database when long-term raw retention is required.
metrics.rollup_retention_description: Set global retention for 1-minute, 5-minute, and 1-hour buckets. Daily buckets follow each metric's retention days, while exact samples remain in memory for 10 minutes. Shorter values are cleaned up by the hourly retention task.
metrics.rollup_retention_invalid: Enter a positive whole number for each bucket retention.
metrics.rollup_retention_order_invalid: Retention must be non-decreasing from 1-minute to 5-minute to 1-hour buckets.
metrics.source_dsn_description: Leave empty to automatically use the previously used monitoring database (default local SQLite ./data/metrics.db) as the source; or enter a source connection string manually. The target is fixed to the currently running monitoring database.
metrics.source_dsn_placeholder: Leave empty to auto-detect, or enter the source DSN
